evidence: A calculation on products: geography's steady annual routing of the design years' runoff over LOLA's 16 pixel/degree heights, with each of the six large seas taking rivers in at its own level and filled towards its lowest pass to another sea. The climate is held at the design years' as the atlas's waters made it; the routing's budget differs from the climate model's, and the model's rain is uncertain by the factor the climate lane carries, so the balances of seas near balance are not settled by it. Not validated against any observation.
reading_rule: Levels in m above the atlas's common level; flows in m3/s; areas in km2 and volumes in km3. A sea's rim is its lowest pass to another sea's water; at it the sea covers every basin its water joins on the way up, listed as basins_joined_below_the_rim. rivers_at_the_rim is what reaches the sea's water at its rim with the other seas at the common level; years_to_fill fills it from the common level on those rivers with its loss to the air growing as it spreads. with_the_seas_above adds what the seas above it pass on once full. budget sets the routing's land runoff, which leaves out land where evaporation exceeds the rain, beside the climate model's own rain less evaporation on the same land.
